The reaction is a Stork enamine synthesis. Cyclohexanone reacts with piperidine (a secondary amine) in the presence of a mild acid catalyst to form an enamine. The enamine then undergoes Michael addition to acrylaldehyde, generating an iminium intermediate. Subsequent hydrolysis with H₃O⁺ yields the 1,5-dicarbonyl product, 3-(2-oxocyclohexyl)propanal. The acid commonly used for enamine formation is p-toluenesulfonic acid (TsOH), as it is strong enough to catalyze dehydration without fully protonating the amine (unlike HCl, which would hinder nucleophilic attack).
